thread:
maria: ran a cross-region failover + replay harness this morning, wanted to capture methodology + surprising perf bits
akash: awesome — quick recap of what you ran?
maria: two modes: 1) synthetic steady qps (poisson) hitting region-a only, 2) replay harness fed from last week's production trace and then simulated drain: region-a drained -> fallback to region-b variants
jen: nice. which model variants? quantized and fp16?
maria: primary model: redwood-medium-fp16-v2, fallback: redwood-medium-q4_v1. kernel combos tested: aten-attn (baseline) vs optimized-kern-v3 (new). batching: dynamic window 10ms vs 30ms. kv-cache warm/cold states toggled.
sam: tl;dr numbers?
maria: short table inline: p50/p95/p99 (latency ms) for replay run, steady 120qps:
- region-a baseline (fp16, opt-ker-v3, window=10ms, kv-warm): 28 / 55 / 130
- region-b fallback (q4, aten, window=10ms, kv-warm): 34 / 75 / 210
- failover moment (drain -> switch): p95 spikes to ~900ms for ~18s in the replay run
leo: 900ms spike — root cause?
maria: profiling traces show 2 contributors: 1) kernel selection mismatch when agent routes to fallback triggers a codepath that falls back to aten kernels and double-copying during quantized dequant path, 2) KV cache misses during the drain: many requests did cold-cache lookups because cache priming wasn't propagated to region-b before traffic cutover
nina: that cache propagation was supposed to be eventual — how many misses?
maria: during the 20s window, cache hit rate dropped from 98%->64%, extra 30-40ms per request on avg on top of kernel delta
jen: batching heuristics? did the 30ms window make anything worse?
maria: yes — with 30ms window, coalescing across inter-region forwarded requests caused head-of-line latencies. region-b had higher RTT so batches waiting for straggler tokens inflated p99. With window=10ms we saw better tail at same throughput but slightly higher CPU efficiency cost.
akash: so multiple interacting factors: kernel path regression + KV coldness + batch stragglers. any perf regression compared to last week's golden run?
maria: compared to golden (same trace, same routes pinned to region-a only): p95 regressed by ~18% in the multi-region failover scenario, p99 up by 60% during failover windows
sam: repro steps so we can run locally?
maria: pasted the harness command we used: 
```
./replay-harness --trace ./prod-trace-2026-03-10.json --qps 120 --drain-schedule 'region-a:60->0@t=300s' --route-policy multi-region-fallback.json --kv-propagation-delay 5s
```
and route-policy snippet: 
```
{ "priority": ["region-a"], "fallback_order": ["region-b"], "model_mapping": {"region-b": "redwood-medium-q4_v1"}}
```
jen: thanks. infra-bot any infra-level logs?
infra-bot: deploys and node counts during test: region-a had 12 pods, region-b had 8 pods. autoscaler didn't spin extra nodes during the 20s spike due to config cooldown of 45s.
leo: autoscaler cooldown explains part of the latency spike too. pre-warming region-b would help.
nina: proposal: three mitigations to test in next run:
1) ensure KV cache priming before cutover (propagate top-K prefixes to target region)
2) add kernel-compatibility check in routing (if fallback model requires aten, prefer model-variant with opt-ker-v3 or do a fast kernel-adapter)
3) reduce batch window for inter-region forwarded traffic to 8-12ms to avoid RTT stragglers
maria: + also temporary tweak: increase autoscaler aggressiveness/cooldown override for failover windows
sam: can you create an experiment matrix? I can run variants in parallel on the harness infra
maria: yes — matrix (short form):
- A: cache-primed + kernel-compat routing + window=10ms
- B: no-priming + kernel-compat + window=10ms
- C: cache-primed + kernel-compat + window=30ms + autoscaler override
- D: baseline (current) for control
jen: what metrics to capture?
maria: must capture p50/p95/p99, kv-hit-rate, kernel-switch-counts, batch-size-dist, cpu/GPU utilization, and tail durations during cutover. Also collect perf profiles: flamegraph + nvtx spans around kernel switch
leo: add a simple A/B apples-to-apples tag: same trace, same total qps, same node counts at start so we can normalize unit economics
akash: owners: maria (experiment orchestration), sam (run harness), jen (profiling + kernel trace), leo (autoscaler tweak), nina (cache priming implementation)
maria: plan to run A/B tomorrow morning 03:00 UTC. I'll push configs to /infra/benchmarks/2026-03-18/ and ping here when started.
replay-bot: scheduled run created: run_id=rb-20260318-01, matrix=A,B,C,D, start=2026-03-18T03:00:00Z
sam: ping me when queued, I'll watch dashboards.
jen: if p99 still bad, next step is to add a temporary circuit-breaker that routes a small fraction to a warm golden model in same region for tail hedging
maria: 👍 added to notes. thanks all — will report results in this thread.
leo: thx, good plan. :thumbsup:
